# Release Notes: v1.0.11

> This file is the source of truth for the GitHub Release body.
> The release workflow (`.github/workflows/release-android.yml`)
> copies this file's contents as the Release body via `body_path`.

## Android

- **Undo now reverses the right day** — Undo just after the day rolled over
  (midnight, or your custom day start) used to take a count off the *new* day,
  or quietly do nothing while the original count stayed. It now always reverses
  the day the count was logged on (#146)
- **Adding a 9th tracker keeps the form open** — at the 8-tracker limit the add
  sheet closed as if it had saved; it now stays open and says why (#146)
- **A pouch price of 0 stays 0** — a saved pouch price of 0 came back as 6.50
  after reopening Settings, and saving again stored 6.50 (#146)
- **Readable sign-in screen** — higher-contrast text on the sign-in screen (#137)

## Web (live once Hosting is deployed)

These ship through Firebase Hosting and need no app update; they are listed
here so this release records everything since v1.0.10.

- **Undo, tracker limit and pouch price** — the same three fixes as Android (#146)
- **Sync problems are no longer hidden** — a failure syncing today's counts now
  shows an error, one healthy update can no longer clear another sync failure,
  and the error banner has a **Retry** button (#146)
- **Export warns if your data changed mid-export** — e.g. a day closed on
  another device while exporting; export again for a consistent copy (#146)
- **Tighter Content Security Policy** — images only from the app itself,
  `data:`/`blob:` and Google profile photos (#143)
- **Privacy notice** — now discloses that the web app loads the Inter font from
  Google Fonts and Google profile photos (#146)

## Release process

- A release that fails after its tag is pushed can now be re-run: the workflow
  resumes at the existing tag (never moved) instead of aborting (#146)

## Not user-visible

Hardening of the not-deployed Option B Cloud Functions (past-date pricing from
stamps only, rate limiting, closed-day-only history edits) (#142, #144).
